items.title: Kalshi chief executive Tarek Mansour defends exchange model in Wall Street Journal op-ed arguing sports contracts are not gambling, Daily Caller reports
items.content_text: - **Kalshi chief executive Tarek Mansour defends exchange model in Wall Street Journal op-ed arguing sports contracts are not gambling, Daily Caller reports** — The Daily Caller reports Kalshi chief executive Tarek Mansour wrote a Wall Street Journal op-ed published October 28, 2026 arguing Kalshi operates a market, not a casino, because customers trade contracts with each other for a fee rather than betting against a house that sets odds. items.title: CFTC sues Utah to protect Kalshi and prediction markets in federal jurisdiction fight, CoinCentral reports
items.content_text: - **CFTC sues Utah to protect Kalshi and prediction markets in federal jurisdiction fight, CoinCentral reports** — CoinCentral reports the CFTC sued the State of Utah and Attorney General Derek Brown in federal court, arguing the state is intruding on federal authority over prediction markets after Utah filed a lawsuit against Kalshi seeking to recover up to 60 million dollars in profits tied to event contracts. The filing is the CFTC's tenth lawsuit against a state over its claimed exclusive jurisdiction, and argues the contracts are swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act offered on CFTC-regulated designated contract markets. items.title: CFTC asks Novig and ProphetX to hold off listing sports micro and scorigami contracts, CryptoWeek reports
items.content_text: - **CFTC asks Novig and ProphetX to hold off listing sports micro and scorigami contracts, CryptoWeek reports** — CryptoWeek reports the CFTC sent letters asking Novig and ProphetX not to list self-certified sports contracts and to explain why they comply with federal commodities law, with neither set yet listed for trading. Novig's micro contracts, such as which player scores the first points in a basketball game, were flagged as susceptible to manipulation, while ProphetX's scorigami contracts, which pay out on a final score never seen before in the sport, were said not to meet the Commodity Exchange Act definition of a swap, and ProphetX said it deferred listing and sent staff further analysis. ([CryptoWeek](https://cryptoweek.ai/news/cftc-asks-novig-and-prophetx-to-hold-off-listing-sports-micro-and-scorigami-contracts-questioning-whether-federal-law-allows-them))

items.content_text: - **Kalshi bans three US candidates for five years for trading on their own races, BitRss reports** — BitRss reports Kalshi suspended Minnesota State Senator Matt Klein, Texas candidate Ezekiel Enriquez and Virginia Senate candidate Mark Moran for trading contracts tied to their own candidacies, describing the cases as political insider trading. Klein was fined 539.85 dollars and Enriquez 784.20 dollars, while Moran received a 6,229.30 dollar penalty and was ordered to return profits, with all three banned for five years. ([BitRss](https://bitrss.com/kalshi-cracks-down-on-political-insider-trading-bans-three-us-candidates-203920))

items.title: CFTC rules split prediction markets from sportsbooks with event contracts as swaps and comments due November 18, CasinoJournal reports
items.content_text: - **CFTC rules split prediction markets from sportsbooks with event contracts as swaps and comments due November 18, CasinoJournal reports** — CasinoJournal reports two CFTC documents published in the Federal Register on Oct. 19 set out the split: sportsbook wagers and casino games are not swaps and belong to state and tribal regulators, while event contracts on sports, politics, culture and weather traded on federally registered exchanges are swaps under the CFTC. The interim exclusion took effect Oct. 19 and the proposed inclusion for 17 CFR 1.3 is not yet in force, with comments on both due Nov. 18. ([CasinoJournal](https://www.casinojournal.com/news/cftc-swap-rules-prediction-markets-sportsbooks))

items.title: Phantom rolls out Kalshi prediction markets to US users as Kalshi October volume reaches 55.33 billion dollars, The Block reports
items.content_text: - **Phantom rolls out Kalshi prediction markets to US users as Kalshi October volume reaches 55.33 billion dollars, The Block reports** — The Block reports Phantom is rolling out Kalshi prediction markets to US users starting Oct. 23, with trades funded using CASH through Phantom Cash accounts at 0.02 dollars per contract plus a network fee and Kalshi KYC required. items.title: Polymarket prices Democrats at 92 percent to flip the House as Kalshi logs 73.4 million House contracts, CoinGape reports
items.content_text: - **Polymarket prices Democrats at 92 percent to flip the House as Kalshi logs 73.4 million House contracts, CoinGape reports** — CoinGape reports Polymarket on Oct. 27 priced Democrats at 92 percent to win the House and 65.5 percent to win the Senate, with Kalshi closely aligned at roughly 90 percent for the House and 64 percent for the Senate. Kalshi alone logged 73.4 million contracts on the House race while Polymarket showed 23.8 million dollars in notional volume on the same market, and Iowa was the sole Senate toss-up with Ashley Hinson at 57.5 percent against Josh Turek at 42 percent. ([CoinGape](https://coingape.com/polymarket-prices-democrats-at-92-to-flip-the-house-as-midterms-loom/))

items.title: Polymarket prices Bitcoin hitting 100,000 dollars by end of year at 17 percent and 110,000 dollars at 9 percent, Moneyweb reports
items.content_text: - **Polymarket prices Bitcoin hitting 100,000 dollars by end of year at 17 percent and 110,000 dollars at 9 percent, Moneyweb reports** — Moneyweb, citing Bloomberg on Oct. 28, reports Bitcoin hovered around 80,800 dollars after reverting from above 87,000 dollars, with Polymarket traders putting the odds of Bitcoin hitting 100,000 dollars by the end of the year at just 17 percent. The chances of a break to 110,000 dollars were priced slimmer still at 9 percent. ([Moneyweb](https://www.moneyweb.co.za/moneyweb-crypto/bitcoin/bitcoins-road-to-100-000-is-crowded-with-would-be-sellers/))
